description: REQ-501(b)'s default-OFF explicit-enable flag is analogized to SOL_GATE_LIVE_ENABLE, but the analogy is a category mismatch, and the resulting failure mode -- a silent, unobserved reversion to idle-permitted behavior -- is never enumerated in the Edge Case Catalog (behavioral-spec.md section 3) despite being the single highest-doctrine-risk scenario this feature exists to prevent. Ground truth: SOL_GATE_LIVE_ENABLE (skills/earn/sol-trade/run.sh:68-75) gates ONLY an additive, shadow-observation exploration layer that sits alongside an ALREADY-always-executing baseline trading pass -- the run.sh comment states verbatim 'it NEVER alters what franklin-trading does below,' i.e. the underlying earn action fires every wake regardless of that flag's state. REQ-501(b), by contrast, gates the entire always-act anti-idle mechanism itself: per its own edge case (behavioral-spec.md:91-92), 'flag unset/malformed/non-1 value: treat as disabled (fail-closed) ... the wake falls through to today's unmodified behavior, including the sleep tool' -- i.e. Franklin's wakes become exactly as idle-capable as before the feature existed. Doctrine (behavioral-spec.md section 0, sourced from memory feedback_franklin_never_waits_always_acts_to_earn) explicitly names this exact condition a failure ('idle/WAIT is a failure signal, not a legitimate outcome ... skip は malware だ'). Section 6 item 10 frames the flag flip as a single deliberate post-vcsdd-converge operational action, which is a defensible one-time rollout gate -- but nothing in REQ-501, REQ-508, or REQ-510 requires any ledger/escalation signal distinguishing 'always-act intentionally not yet enabled' from 'always-act silently regressed to OFF after go-live due to a config/deploy/.env bug.' REQ-508's escalation path only fires INSIDE an already-engaged always-act wake when both bounds are exhausted -- it has no visibility into a wake where always-act failed to engage at all. For a feature whose entire premise is that Franklin idling is money-doctrine-critical, this is a real, uncovered edge case.
